newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures up slightly, pause before CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures up slightly, pause before CPI.

text.p: U.S. debt futures held slim gains from Friday's sharp rally, as the market paused ahead of the U.S. May Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Tuesday, traders and analysts said.
"The market is waiting for news to drive it," one T-bond futures trader said. "But we have a better chance of making highs, than hitting lows ahead of CPI."
Overall and core CPI are seen rising 0.2 percent.
Light selling after the opening bell kept September T-bonds from testing the 3-1/2-month high of 112-02/32, traders said. The contract rose to 112-00 overnight.
"People are probing levels, but the market is just rangebound," another bond futures floor source said.
Eurodollar futures sources also reported lackluster conditions, as traders squared positions from the market's rally off of the weak May Producer Price Index (PPI).
May PPI fell 0.3 percent both overall and in the core rate, versus average trade estimates for up 0.1 percent in both rates.
One Eurodollar futures analyst said December began pricing out another U.S. rate hike as it climbed towards 94.00 on Friday.
December will price in a neutral Fed policy once it tests the 94.25 level, one analyst said.
While most analysts said December is technically poised to test 94.25 in the longer term, they said the CPI data on Tuesday could change the scenario.
Traders said December could fall through support at 93.95 to 93.92 if CPI posts larger-than-expected gains from April's rise of 0.1 percent overall and 0.3 percent excluding food and energy.
Support for September T-bonds is at 111-16/32, which corresponds to a cash long bond yield of 6.75 percent.
Support also rests at Friday's pit session low of 111-11/32.
However, traders look for both September bonds and December Eurodollars to trade at the upper end of Friday's ranges after closing at 3-1/2-month highs.
In addition, the Commodity Research Bureau's Index fell slightly, solidifying ideas that the U.S. inflation rate is in no danger of rising in any time soon, they said.
One trader said trading in Eurodollars could pick up later in the week due to several asset-backed security deals.
September T-bonds started to grind higher, testing Friday's high of 112-02/32 in light volume, one trader said.

Resistance for September T-bonds is at 112-11/32, a retracement level from the contract's six-and-a-half month downmove. September also faces resistance at 113-01/32, its highest settlement price in six months.

At 0913 CDT/1413 GMT, September T-bonds were up 07/32 at 112-02/32, 10-yr notes were 03/32 higher to 108-16/32, munibonds rose 04/32 to 117-30/32, Sept T-bills were up 0.02 at 94.81, and December Eurodollars rose 0.005 to 93.97. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
